function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure! Here’s a quick rundown of places you can order a cake from—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or just a convenient delivery service:

| Type | What it offers | How to get it | Tips |
|------|----------------|---------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Freshly baked cakes, custom designs, seasonal flavors | Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Yelp; many have their own websites or Instagram pages | Call ahead to confirm availability & delivery hours; ask about special dietary needs (gluten‑free, vegan, nut‑allergy friendly). |
| **Grocery chains** | Ready‑made cakes, birthday specials, seasonal items | Visit the bakery section in supermarkets (Walmart, Kroger, Safeway, Publix, etc.) or order online via their website/app | Great for last‑minute orders; check if they offer same‑day pickup or delivery. |
| **Online marketplaces** | Wide variety of cakes from local bakers, national brands, and specialty shops | Use platforms like **Amazon Fresh**, **Instacart**, or **Google Shopping** to compare prices and delivery times | Look at seller ratings and read recent reviews; note shipping fees and delivery windows. |
| **Food‑delivery apps** | Cakes from restaurants, cafés, and independent bakeries | Order through **Uber Eats**, **DoorDash**, **Postmates**, **Grubhub**, or **Caviar** | Many apps let you filter by “dessert” or “cakes”; check delivery fees and tip policies. |
| **Specialty cake makers** | Custom designs, themed cakes, premium ingredients | Search for “custom cake shop” + your city; many have dedicated websites (e.g., Cake Boss, Sweet Treats, or local artisan bakers) | Ideal for birthdays, weddings, or corporate events; book early (especially during holidays). |
| **Subscription boxes** | Monthly cake deliveries (often artisanal or themed) | Sign up for services like **Goldbelly**, **The Cake Box**, or local subscription services | Good for regular treats or gifting; check cancellation policies. |

### Quick Steps to Place an Order

1. **Decide on the occasion & budget** – This helps narrow down choices (birthday, wedding, office party, etc.).
2. **Choose a platform** – Local bakeries for freshness, delivery apps for convenience, or specialty shops for unique designs.
3. **Check delivery options** – Same‑day, next‑day, or scheduled delivery. Some services allow you to set a delivery time window.
4. **Place the order** – Provide details such as size, flavor, design preferences, and any dietary restrictions.
5. **Confirm & pay** – Most platforms accept credit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, or Google Pay. Keep the receipt or confirmation email handy.
6. **Track the order** – Delivery apps usually provide real‑time tracking; local bakeries may call or text when the cake is on its way.

---

#### Need help finding a place near you?

If you tell me your city or ZIP code, I can look up specific bakeries, delivery partners, or even recommend a few top‑rated spots based on recent reviews. Just let me know!
